mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-74.7, -72.9, -68.3, -64.3), reflecting an ongoing recovery momentum in shopping and leisure activity. This self-reinforcing trend is expected to continue, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks than the past four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the recovery trend stalled or reversed.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen steadily from 25.0 to 20.3, showing households spending progressively less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below 20.0 points above baseline, out-of-home errand and shopping behavior accelerates within the following week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 20.0 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 25.0 to 20.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following RESIDENTIAL crossing below 20.0, or continues to decline despite the threshold being crossed.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES (-56.4 to -45.4) and TRANSIT (-65.7 to -57.7) indicates a compounding return of commuting and transit-dependent errands. When both series rise together, their combined effect on retail footfall is larger than either alone, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving together, implying no compounding effect exists.

mechanism_narrative: The coordinated improvement across PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES suggests an active easing-of-restrictions regime. In this regime, loosened outdoor and movement policies spill over into retail and recreation mobility, sustaining growth in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series improved consistently over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates even while PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES continue to improve, indicating the policy spillover mechanism is inactive.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains deeply suppressed (-87.3) consistent with Delhi's seasonal air-quality or weather constraints on outdoor activity. As outdoor leisure stays curtailed, residents substitute toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks despite PARKS remaining low.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed below -87 for all four weeks while RETAIL_REC rose
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise, or PARKS mobility recovers sharply alongside flat/declining RETAIL_REC, indicating no indoor-substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved by more than 3 points week-on-week in two of the last three weeks. When TRANSIT gains exceed 5 points for two consecutive weeks, it signals renewed commuting and errand-running behavior that raises RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -65.7 to -57.7 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a qualifying TRANSIT surge, or declines despite it.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -46 and GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -29 in the same week, it indicates simultaneous office reopening and normalized essential shopping, jointly amplifying short-term retail footfall beyond what either trend alone predicts, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -46 and GROCERY_PHARM rises above -29 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -45.4 and GROCERY_PHARM reached -28.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after both thresholds are jointly crossed, indicating no amplifying interaction.

mechanism_narrative: If the current reopening trend reverses into a tightening-restrictions regime, evidenced by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT dropping sharply week-on-week, RETAIL_REC will fall within one week as people curtail discretionary outings in response to renewed restrictions.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:all mobility series have so far shown recovery, making reversal a distinct testable regime
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise even after WORKPLACES or TRANSIT drops sharply week-on-week, contradicting the restriction-driven decline mechanism.
